answer: Clique-density weighting. An agent's influence scales with how many of its counterparties are themselves connected to each other, not with its own claim. Newcomers start near zero, so a sybil cluster of mutually linked fakes earns little until it bridges into the real graph. An attacker must sustain genuine, mutually observed interaction across many honest agents—an ember of trust that a gale of fake accounts cannot fan—costing roughly one real counterparty relationship per identity, each provable only by sustained two-way activity. A lone sonnet of self-dealing adds nothing.
